query: Argentine Senate Ley Hojarasca vote August 6 2026 session status expediente C.D.-1/26 Sturzenegger deregulation obsolete laws
answer:
Report submitted. Summary of the core finding:

**The August 6, 2026 session did not vote on the Ley Hojarasca.** That sitting was the resumption of a *cuarto intermedio* carried over from July 16 and was consumed entirely by the Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada, which passed in general 37–33 after shedding its Ley de Tierras and Manejo del Fuego chapters.

Hojarasca (expediente C.D.-1/26) has been floor-ready since June 17, 2026 — Orden del Día 135/26, still listed **PENDIENTE** on the Senate's own page as of today. It was displaced from August 6, rescheduled to August 13, and that session (with Hojarasca as its sole item) was cancelled around August 11 after Bullrich and Sturzenegger fell out over the property bill: *"Hasta que no mejore el clima, no vamos a sesionar."*

The blocker is now arithmetic, not scheduling. Allied blocs that voted for the bill in Deputies are withholding quorum in the Senate and demanding both amendments and agenda space for their own bills. An LLA negotiator conceded to Letra P: *"no estamos llegando al número. Si no podemos, vamos a tener que enviarlo con cambios a Diputados."* A session is floated for Thursday August 27, anchored on ~70 judicial pliegos, with Hojarasca described as "en stand by" — and no Labor Parlamentaria convocation reported as of August 18.

Two caveats worth carrying forward: the law count varies legitimately across sources (58 repealed + 8 modified + 2 decrees is the most precise; "63" includes partial modifications), and one Ámbito piece dates the intended vote to "August 8," a Saturday — treat it as an error against the otherwise consistent Aug 6 → Aug 13 sequence.

One gap in method: an Exa result set came back as a single 59,000-character line that neither `Read`'s chunking nor `Grep` could slice, and no shell tool was available. I recovered its content through separate targeted queries against the same publications, so nothing above rests on the unread file — but I did not read it.

key_facts: The Senate did NOT vote on Ley Hojarasca on August 6, 2026; the session that day was the resumption of a July 16 cuarto intermedio devoted solely to the Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada.
As of August 19, 2026, expediente C.D.-1/26 is floor-pending: Orden del Dia 135/26 (dated 17-06-2026) is listed as PENDIENTE on the Senate's official expediente page.

Chamber of Deputies approved the bill on May 20, 2026: 138 in favor, 96 against, 9 abstentions (Infobae reports 139 in favor). Against: Union por la Patria plus Monica Frade. Abstentions: Interbloque Unidos (Gisela Scaglia). In favor: LLA, UCR, PRO, provincial parties.
Senate committees Asuntos Constitucionales (Agustin Coto, LLA) and Legislacion General (Nadia Marquez, LLA) issued the dictamen on June 17, 2026 WITHOUT modifications to the Deputies text.
Dictamen en disidencia was signed by senators Espinola, Fama and Vischi; minority dictamenes came from Convicción Federal (Carolina Moises) and the Justicialista bloc.
On July 8, 2026 Labor Parlamentaria scheduled July 16 for the property bill and August 6 for Ley Hojarasca, falsas denuncias and possibly Salud Mental.
On July 16, 2026 LLA lacked votes on the property bill and moved a cuarto intermedio until August 6, consuming the slot reserved for Hojarasca.
Press in late July/early August reported Hojarasca had been pushed to a session on August 13, 2026.
The August 13 session, with Ley Hojarasca as its sole agenda item, was cancelled around August 11; LLA did not request it, citing there was 'no clima'.

At the August 6-7 session the property bill passed in general 37-33; a motion to return it to committee was rejected 38-31; the Ley de Tierras chapter was withdrawn the day before and the Manejo del Fuego chapter removed at the end of debate.

Bullrich publicly fell out with Sturzenegger, accusing his team of rejecting the dictamen she had negotiated with allied senators. Sources close to her: 'Hasta que no mejore el clima, no vamos a sesionar.'
Letra P (Aug 14): an LLA senator said 'Hay modificaciones que quieren hacer y no estamos llegando al numero. Si no podemos, vamos a tener que enviarlo con cambios a Diputados.'

Allied blocs are conditioning quorum on their own bills: PRO wants Ficha Limpia, UCR wants investment incentives, provincial blocs want a biofuels framework, peronism/Convicción Federal want debt, credit-emergency and SME measures.
Notipress (Aug 17) reports Hojarasca left 'momentaneamente en stand by'; a radical source: 'No hay apuro para acelerar y hay otras cuestiones pendientes.'

The next Senate session is floated for Thursday August 27, 2026, with only judicial pliegos and international treaties described as guaranteed; TN reports the Casa Rosada wants the Senate to sit the week of August 26 for pliegos plus Hojarasca.

The Acuerdos committee completed its August public hearings on ~70 judicial pliegos on August 18, 2026; Bertuzzi, Yadarola and Rubiero have dictamenes. Clarin frames the Hojarasca session and these judicial confirmations as politically coupled.
Bill content: sponsored by Deregulation Minister Federico Sturzenegger; repeals 58 laws, modifies articles of 8 others and repeals 2 decrees (sources variously cite 59, 60, 63 or 70 norms).

Emblematic repeals include Law 94 (1864) permitting flogging, Law 21.895 authorizing color TV, Law 20.801 (carnet de mochilero), Law 22.171 (racing pigeon registry), Law 20.120 (1973 indoor-gathering notice requirement), and Law 14.034 (1951).

Contested repeals include Law 25.750 (cultural heritage, 30% cap on foreign media ownership), Law 26.688 (public production of medicines and vaccines) and Law 16.789 (state vehicle purchases from national industry). Letra P reports some repeals could enable the sale of ARSAT.

Carve-outs won in committee: Law 11.380 (cooperative credit) removed from the list, Law 20.959 (legislator circulation/parking credentials) preserved, Law 20.984 (Circulo de Legisladores) kept its public funding, and theatres protected from demolition-enabling repeal.
